nodes.label: AI-Assisted Legacy Application Modernization Platform
nodes.description: 13-slide student project deck (Full Stack Development, Dept. of IT, Easwari Engineering College) proposing a platform that parses legacy code into ASTs, extracts control-flow and data-flow semantics into a language-agnostic IR, and uses AST-guided LLMs to generate equivalent, maintainable code in modern languages, validated by generated tests and behavioral comparison.
nodes.rationale: Manual rewrites are expensive and risky, and simple transpilers miss the intent of complex legacy logic, so the platform first understands code structurally, then reasons about its semantics, then generates code; this reduces dependence on scarce legacy-language experts while keeping engineering teams in control. Structural parsing and analysis ground the AI step and automated validation closes the loop, preserving semantic fidelity end to end.

nodes.label: Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
nodes.description: Tree representation that captures the exact structural and syntactic form of legacy source code; produced by the AST Parser and used to ground both semantic analysis and LLM code generation.
nodes.rationale: Treating code as a structured program rather than text is what makes translation structure-aware instead of line-by-line text substitution.

nodes.label: Control-Flow Analysis
nodes.description: Extraction of control-flow semantics from the AST by the semantic analysis layer; complex control flow is where rule-based transpilers tend to mistranslate.

nodes.label: Data-Flow Analysis
nodes.description: Extraction of data-flow and data-dependency information from the AST, feeding the intermediate representation.

nodes.label: Language-Agnostic Intermediate Representation (IR)
nodes.description: Language-agnostic representation of program behavior built by the semantic analyzer from control-flow, data-flow and dependency information and passed to the AI code generation engine (the abstract's 'intermediate-representation mapping').

nodes.label: Static Analysis
nodes.description: One of the three techniques the platform combines, alongside IR mapping and generative AI; realized by the AST parsing and semantic analysis stages.

nodes.label: Large Language Models (LLMs)
nodes.description: Generative AI models that, guided by the AST and semantic context, synthesize equivalent idiomatic code in the target language and framework; used through LLM APIs or local inference (optional GPU with 8GB+ VRAM).

nodes.label: Structure- and Semantic-Aware Translation
nodes.description: Core principle: translation reasons over program structure (AST) and control-flow/data-flow semantics instead of raw text or line-by-line substitution (abstract callout 'Structure-aware' and key capability 'Semantic-Aware').
nodes.rationale: Existing tools treat source code largely as text, so they cannot reason about program intent, data dependencies, or cross-module relationships.

nodes.label: Legacy Codebase
nodes.description: Pipeline input: decades-old, mission-critical code in COBOL, PL/I, VB6 or aging Java/C++ that is costly to maintain, hard to extend and increasingly hard to staff for.

nodes.label: AST Parser
nodes.description: Pipeline stage 1 (Parse): turns legacy source into an AST through a modular parser layer with pluggable per-language grammars (COBOL, VB6, Java, C++).
nodes.rationale: The parser layer is modular so additional legacy languages can be supported without redesigning the AI generation engine.

nodes.label: Semantic Analyzer (IR)
nodes.description: Pipeline stage 2 (Analyze): extracts control-flow, data-flow and dependency information from the AST and builds a language-agnostic intermediate representation.

nodes.label: AI Code Generation Engine (LLM)
nodes.description: Pipeline stage 3 (Generate): LLMs guided by the AST and semantic context (IR) synthesize equivalent, idiomatic code in the target language and framework; the deck's 'AST-driven AI code generation'.
nodes.rationale: Grounding generation in the AST preserves program structure and business logic more faithfully than text-based translation.

nodes.label: Automated Validation & Tests (Built-In Validation)
nodes.description: Pipeline stage 4 (Validate): generated code is checked automatically through unit test generation and behavioral comparison against the original system before developer review; presented as the 'Built-In Validation' advantage.
nodes.rationale: Catching regressions early raises confidence in migrated code and closes the loop before code reaches production.
nodes.stage_category: Static parsing & structure (per the Slide 11 legend)

nodes.label: Modernized Application
nodes.description: Pipeline output: equivalent, idiomatic code in a modern language and framework that keeps the business logic while improving readability, testability and long-term maintainability.

nodes.label: Automated Unit Test Generation
nodes.description: Automatic generation of unit tests for the generated code, one of the two validation techniques.

nodes.label: Behavioral Comparison Against Original System
nodes.description: Validation technique that compares the generated code's behavior with the original legacy system to catch functional regressions.

nodes.label: Multi-Language Scalability
nodes.description: Key capability and advantage: COBOL, VB6, Java and C++ are parsed through pluggable grammars, and the modular parser layer lets new legacy languages be added without redesigning the AI generation engine.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop Review
nodes.description: Key capability: every generated change can be reviewed by developers before merge; developer review follows automated validation.
nodes.rationale: Keeps engineering teams in control of the transformation.

nodes.label: Existing Legacy Modernization Approaches
nodes.description: Current practice: manual rewriting by domain experts, rule-based transpilers, and pattern-matching migration scripts, which treat source code largely as text rather than as a structured program with well-defined semantics.

nodes.label: Manual Rewriting
nodes.description: Domain experts re-implement legacy logic by hand in a modern language: accurate, but slow, costly and risky.

nodes.label: Rule-Based Transpilers
nodes.description: Fixed syntax-to-syntax mapping rules: fast, but brittle when code deviates from expected patterns, and prone to missing the intent of complex legacy logic.

nodes.label: Pattern-Matching Migration Scripts
nodes.description: Regular-expression or template scripts that convert common code blocks but fail on complex or undocumented logic.

nodes.label: High Manual Effort
nodes.description: Disadvantage: manual rewriting needs extensive developer time and deep legacy-language expertise that is increasingly scarce.

nodes.label: Loss of Business Logic
nodes.description: Disadvantage: rule-based transpilers often mistranslate complex control flow, risking silent functional regressions.

nodes.label: Poor Scalability
nodes.description: Disadvantage: existing approaches do not scale across millions of lines of legacy code spanning multiple languages.

nodes.label: Limited Semantic Understanding
nodes.description: Disadvantage: text-based tools cannot reason about program intent, data dependencies, or cross-module relationships.

nodes.label: Higher Translation Accuracy
nodes.description: Advantage: grounding code generation in the AST preserves program structure and business logic more faithfully than text-based translation, matching the abstract's goal of preserving business logic.

nodes.label: Reduced Manual Effort
nodes.description: Advantage: automating structural analysis and code synthesis cuts the developer hours spent on migration; the abstract claims a potential 60%+ reduction in manual rewrite effort.
nodes.note: The 60%+ figure is stated as a potential reduction; the deck gives no measurement or source for it.

nodes.label: Chen et al. 2021 - Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (Codex)
nodes.description: Trained large language models on code (Codex) to generate functions from context. Pro: strong code synthesis from pre-trained transformers. Con: struggles with long, stateful legacy logic without structural guidance.
nodes.citation: M. Chen et al., 'Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code,' arXiv:2107.03374, 2021 (Reference 1).
nodes.norm_label: chen et al. 2021 - evaluating large language models trained on code (codex)

nodes.label: Feng et al. 2020 - CodeBERT
nodes.description: CodeBERT, a bimodal pre-trained model for code and natural language. Pro: better code search, documentation and translation. Con: not designed for full program migration or AST-level reasoning.
nodes.citation: Z. Feng et al., 'CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages,' Proc. EMNLP Findings, 2020 (Reference 2).

nodes.label: Rodriguez et al. 2022 - Survey of Rule-Based Transpilers
nodes.description: Surveyed rule-based transpilers for legacy-to-modern code migration. Pro: established a baseline for automated syntactic translation. Con: fails on ambiguous or undocumented legacy patterns.
nodes.note: Cited only in the Literature Survey: it is absent from the Slide 12 References and no title or venue is given, so this label is descriptive.
nodes.norm_label: rodriguez et al. 2022 - survey of rule-based transpilers

nodes.label: Kumar et al. 2023 - AST Representations with LLMs for Guided Refactoring
nodes.description: Combined AST-based program representations with LLMs for guided refactoring. Pro: better semantic accuracy than pure prompt-based generation. Con: needs robust parsers per legacy language, adding overhead.
nodes.note: Cited only in the Literature Survey: it is absent from the Slide 12 References and no title or venue is given, so this label is descriptive.
nodes.norm_label: kumar et al. 2023 - ast representations with llms for guided refactoring
